chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you reach al-Aqiq from the direction of Iraq, or reach one of these miqat stations, and you intend to enter the state of Ihram, Allah willing, then pluck your armpits, clip your nails, remove your pubic hair, and trim your moustache, and it does not harm you whichever of these you begin with. Then brush your teeth, perform ghusl, and wear your two garments, and let your completion of these acts be, Allah willing, at the decline of the sun (midday); and if it is not at the decline of the sun, it does not harm you, except that I love for it to be with choice at the decline of the sun.

key_terms.الِاسْتِثْنَاك: Brushing the teeth (from the root s-t-n-k)
key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: Ihram, the sacred state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْعَقِيق: Al-Aqiq, a specific miqat station for residents of Iraq
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيت: Miqat stations, designated places where pilgrims enter the state of Ihram
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْس: The decline of the sun, referring to midday when the sun passes its zenith

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended grooming acts and timing for entering Ihram according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the preparatory grooming (sunan al-ihram) required before entering the sacred state, emphasizing that the sequence of acts such as clipping nails and shaving pubic hair is flexible. It specifically recommends performing these rituals and assuming Ihram at midday (zawal al-shams), reflecting the scholarly preference for aligning ritual purity with the time of Dhuhr prayer to ensure spiritual readiness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, altogether from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you end up to Al-Aqeeq from the direction of Al-Iraq, or to a juncture from these junctures, and you are intending (to wear) the Ihraam, Allahazwj Willing, so pluck your armpits, and clip your nails, and clear your pubic hair, and take (off) from your moustache, and it does not harm you by which of that you begin with. Then, brush your teeth, and wash, and wear your clothes, and let yourself be free from doing that, Allahazwj Willing, by the (start of the) decline of the sun (midday); and if that cannot happen by the decline of the sun, so it would not harm you. Iasws would love it if that happens with the choice by the (start of the) decline of the sun’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from ibn abu ‘Umayr all from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you arrive at al-‘Aqiq from the side of Iraq you should clean your underarms, cut your fingers nails, cleanse your pubic hairs with a certain paste and trim your mustache. It is not harmful whichever you do first. In addition, you should do so at any of designated Mawaqit (places for assuming the state of Ihram) when you are about to assume the state of Ihram by the will of Allah. Thereafter brush your teeth and put on your two pieces of cloths. You should complete it by the will of Allah near Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime). If it is not at this time it is not harmful; however, I like it to be at that time if there is not any emergency.’”
